olivia: Heads up — saw a latency spike on prod dedicated for a transformer with head_dim=22 on an A100 pool. Flashv3 causal picker routed to a slow path and eventually fell back to the generic SDPA kernel, 3x token latency for a short period. Anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:
sam: ugh. can you paste the picker log? is this across multiple seqlens or just short ones?
olivia: log snippet:```[2026-03-12 14:02:11] kernel_picker: model=rwkv-8b head_dim=22 seqlen=64 sm=80 picked=flashv3_noncausal reason=unsupported_headmod -> fallback=generic_sdpa time_ms=2.8``` looks like it marked it non-causal then fallback. spike only for seqlen <= 128 in that job.
jin: head_dim=22 is an oddball. flash kernels expect head_dim % 8 == 0 or at least aligned to 4 for some kernels. flashv3 added a bunch of head-remap heuristics — might be misclassifying causal vs non-causal when head stride padding is required.
mika: did the autotuner probe list include that exact head_dim/stride on sm80? We sometimes skip tiny headwidths in the probe to avoid jitter; that means we can lack a valid flashv3 causal candidate and end up on generic.
olivia: repro command (ran on a small dedicated node):```python -m rwinference.run_profile --model rwkv-8b --batch 8 --seqlen 64 --head-dim 22 --profile-kernelpicker --device a100``` got the picker dump + nvprof traces. attaching full traces to the thread.
sam: can you paste the kernelpicker decision table for that run? especially the autotune probe results and fallback thresholds.
olinia: (typo) sorry, attachment uploaded -> picker.json.gz
jin: quick theory: flashv3 causal requires contiguous head layout after remap; when head_dim < 32 the remap algorithm picks a microkernel variant that we haven't validated on sm80 for int8/quant runs. fallback is triggered because the kernel reports unsupported by kernel feature test. Two fixes: 1) add a synthetic probe entry for head_dim in the autotuner to record performance; 2) relax the feature-test to allow a slightly slower but stable flashv3 causal kernel on these odd widths.
mika: i prototyped a hysteresis patch to the selector last week: increase stability window for headmod changes -> prevents bouncing between flash and generic during short bursts. diff:```diff -- a/kernel_picker/selectors.py +++ b/kernel_picker/selectors.py @@ -212,7 +212,9 @@ class HeadModSelector:     def pick(self, features):-        if features.head_mod_change_recent:             return fallback_kernel+        # add hysteresis for tiny head dims+        if features.head_dim < 32 and features.recent_success_rate < 0.7:+            return fallback_kernel``` this reduced flips in local sim.
perf-bot: [automated] anomaly detected: kernel_fallback_rate increased from 0.3% -> 4.8% for rwkv-8b (head_dim=22) between 2026-03-12T13:58 and 2026-03-12T14:05. Linked trace: https://perf.redwood.internal/traces/2623456789
sam: can we add a short-term guard: if head_dim % 4 != 0 then prefer generic_sdpa until tuner collects stats? we trade some p99 for stability.
jin: agree for short term. long term we should expand probe matrix: add head_dim values [10,14,18,22,26] and run nightly microbenchmarks on sm80/sm86/sm90. also log remap path and kernel capability result so we can see why the feature-test failed.
mika: i'll ship the hysteresis + a config flag to force generic for nonaligned heads behind a rollout. canary to 5% of rwkv jobs.
olivia: cool — action items: mika will open PR with hysteresis + rollout flag; jin will add probe entries and feature-test logging; sam will monitor p95/p99 and fallback rate. I'll coordinate canary. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
